label: Christoph Benzmüller and Bruno…, Gödel's…: AFP GoedelGod.thy, theorem Monotheism: at every world…
locator: GoedelGod.thy, Monotheism: "[∀(λx.∀(λy. (G x m→ (G y m→ (x mL= y)))))]"
interpretation: Theorem Monotheism, glossed in the theory as 'There is only one God: any two God-like beings are equal', proved there by (metis Flawlessness G_def). 'Equal' is the theory's mL=, Leibniz equality x mL= y ≡ ∀(λφ. (φ x m→ φ y)), evaluated at a world. Because this embedding quantifies over all properties, that relation implies identity of individuals, by instantiating the property with fun z _ => x = z. Monotheism establishes at most one God-like individual per world. It does not establish existence by itself; with corollary C2, it establishes exactly one per world. Neither conclusion asserts that the individual is the same across worlds. Attributed to the AFP formalization of Scott's notes, not to what Scott or Gödel intended.
